14.0.s.en: (1) The fear of the people and the encouragement of Joshua and Caleb

14.0.0.en: As a result of the bad report that the ten spies brought to the people, great fear, regret and anguish arose. Most of the people did not sleep that night, but came out of their tents in weeping, crying and wailing, and as usual they murmured and put all the blame on Moses and Aaron. This shows us how fickle this people was and how quickly evil spreads. Although they stood on the threshold of the land God had promised, in their great despair they wished that they had died in the land of Egypt or in the wilderness of Sinai, which would be better than facing these mighty enemies, the inhabitants of the land of Canaan.

14.0.1.en: v. 3 (with): Their murmuring and their lack of faith increased, despite the great miracles God had worked among them. They raised their murmuring to a level higher than Moses and Aaron, for they murmured against God Himself, and in a regrettable manner they criticized the wisdom of God and His plan. In their distress they said brazenly: Would it not be better for us to return and be enslaved in Egypt?! For obeying God, they said, means that we die at the hands of our enemies, who will take our children and our women captive.

14.1.0.en: As the weeping, crying and murmuring spread and grew, some of them called out with a strange idea, which was to depose Moses and Aaron and appoint a new head over the people to lead them in their return to Egypt, forgetting that the true leader is God, who leads them through the pillar of cloud and guides them through His speaking with Moses. But this is how anger blinds a man from seeing the facts and the obvious.

14.2.0.en: As for Moses and Aaron, they fell on the ground before God. This means their helplessness with the people and their taking refuge in God, so they humbled themselves before Him that He might bring them and this people through this critical situation.

14.2.1.en: Let us all beware of anger, its results, and the rising of agitation within us, for the wrath of man does not work the righteousness of God, but usually leads him to a folly of which he repents afterward. So let us take refuge in God by prayer when distress comes upon us, and leave the matter in His hand, confident that He always gives and does for us what is best.

14.3.0.en: Rent their clothes: an act expressing grief, sorrow and severe distress.

14.3.1.en: Here we see another face and a positive direction of thinking. Joshua the son of Nun, together with Caleb the son of Jephunneh, stood facing the people, declaring their objection and their grief at what they had seen of the people, and they rent their clothes in grief and anger at and over this people who had forgotten all of God's previous work.

14.4.0.en: Both of them began to speak and tried to persuade and encourage the people that this land, that is, the land of Canaan, is a good and wonderful land which cannot be left or given up. It is a land whose goodness overflows with milk and honey, as they had told the people before (ch. 13:27), and if God is pleased with them, He will give them this land as an inheritance for them and for their children.

14.5.0.en: For they are bread for us: we shall defeat them, take their spoil and eat it as we eat bread.

14.5.1.en: This land will become ours and we shall defeat its peoples, because the Lord our God is with us and has delivered them to us, so do not fear anything.

14.5.2.en: Their defence is departed from them: an expression meaning that God has removed His protection from these peoples, and therefore it is easy to defeat them.

14.6.0.en: The insolence and murmuring reached their height, and instead of listening to Joshua and Caleb, the faithful witnesses, the people turned the more against them and even demanded that they be stoned to death. When God saw all this murmuring, and even the attempt to kill Joshua and Caleb, He intervened swiftly and appeared in His glory in the tabernacle to all the people.

14.7.0.en: The Lord began His speech with Moses, declaring His anger at the people and showing Moses the great evil into which they had fallen. The Lord showed His anger by using a hard expression, for He regarded what the people had done as an insult to His holy person. Their murmuring was unbelief in the power of God, or disbelief of His holy promises, and a lack of acknowledgment and thanks for all that He had previously done for them.

14.8.0.en: God declared to Moses the punishment He was about to carry out, namely a plague He would send to destroy the people, and He would make of Moses and Aaron and the faithful among the people a new beginning for a new people, greater and larger in number, as He did with Noah before at the renewal of creation. For God in His justice does not include all in His punishment, but the sinners alone. As for those who were faithful and kept His covenants, God preserves them from the hard trial and does not punish them.

14.9.0.en: Moses, the loving one, the intercessor and advocate for his people, began to plead and defend them, for it greatly troubled him that the people should be destroyed. Overcome by his love for his people, he spoke with God, saying: You have brought up, O my God, by Your strong arm this people from the land of Egypt, and You taught all peoples that You have become our leader and king and that You dwell in our midst. We, Your people, have seen You face to face, and we saw Your glory on Mount Horeb; You overshadowed us with Your cloud and led us by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire by day and by night.

14.10.0.en: If it should happen that You carry out Your punishment by the destruction of this people, will not the Egyptians, and with them all the peoples who heard of Your previous works with us and then of Your chastisement of Your people, say that their God did not fulfill for them His promise, which He had promised, to bring them into the land, but on the contrary destroyed them and got rid of them in the desert?!

14.11.0.en: Let the power of my Lord be great: an expression of praise and glorification of God and an introduction to what Moses is about to ask of God.

14.11.1.en: Moses gives God the glory, for He alone is almighty and in His hand are all judgments, and he reminds Him of His previous promises which He made with His people on the mountain and which are recorded in (Ex 34:6, 7).

14.12.0.en: These words, which God had spoken before and which Moses uses here, are, as we have said, a review of what God said, namely:

14.12.1.en: The LORD is longsuffering: You have already declared, O God, Your mercies and Your long-suffering toward Your people, and we hold fast to this as a promise from You to us, and we now ask that it be fulfilled in us.

14.12.2.en: Forgiving iniquity: that is, You pardon Your people and forget their sin if they come to You repentant, which accords and agrees with the Master who is gracious and generous to His servants.

14.12.3.en: And by no means clearing the guilty, but visiting...: that is, God is also just in the case of the impenitence of His servants, for His wide and abundant mercies go side by side with His justice. The expression “the iniquity of the fathers upon the children” means that in many cases the children reap the result of the bad conduct of the fathers, like spendthrift fathers who squander their inheritance and leave their children in poverty, or hereditary diseases of which the wayward fathers are the cause for their children. But this saying is not absolute, as evidenced by the fact that God punished the people who sinned by not letting them enter the land, yet those under twenty years of age did not suffer the punishment but entered the land of promise. In sum, God declares the breadth of His mercies toward repentant sinners and the severity of His justice toward the refusing and the disobedient. What is meant also by visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children is the children's walking in evil like their fathers, so that He punishes them in His justice for their evils, which they acquired from their fathers and which extended through the generations.

14.13.0.en: Moses continues in his entreaty and intercession with God for the people, and asks Him to have mercy on them and forgive their sin as His grace and divine salvation, regardless of whether this people deserves this forgiveness or not!! He also reminds God that this is nothing new to His fatherly heart, for He had already forgiven His people many times since their departure from the land of Egypt.

14.13.1.en: May we all possess this loving heart of the prophet Moses, so that we learn to pray for everyone, especially those who do wrong and those who are far away, and ask God's mercies for all. For one of the things that most rejoices the heart of God is that we pray for those who do wrong and those who are far away before we pray for ourselves.

14.14.s.en: (3) The Lord's speech to Moses and the answer to his intercession

14.14.0.en: God's answer comes as very joyful to Moses, for He declares His forgiveness and pardon of His people. In His wonderful humility and His exalting of the accepted intercession of Moses, God says to him, “according to thy word.” What honor, then, belongs to the holy men of God! God forgives the people here for the sake of Moses' request, and again He shuts up the heaven so that it does not rain, as Elijah asked?!

14.15.0.en: As I live: a form of oath and affirmation equal to the expression “I have sworn by Myself.”

14.15.1.en: God continues His speech with Moses, saying: Although I have answered your request for forgiveness, My glory, which fills the whole earth, also requires that I execute My justice. This verse is considered an introduction to God's sentence in the coming verses.

14.16.0.en: As for God's justice, His judgment was as follows: the whole generation that had seen God's power and His lofty arm and how He brought them out of the land of Egypt would be punished by not seeing the land that God promised to their fathers, and they would not enter it and possess it. God gives as the reason this generation did not deserve this grace that they insulted Him greatly, having tempted Him ten times, and yet they murmured against Him. “Ten times” means many times, but literally also they tried Him in the ten plagues in the land of Egypt, and also ten times in different places, which we show here by mentioning ten occasions on which the people tried God and His power, though the meaning intended is that they tempted Me many times.

14.16.1.en: 1- The killing of the firstborn of the Egyptians and the preservation of their own firstborn.

14.16.2.en: 2- When they crossed the Red Sea and Pharaoh and all his armies pursued them (Ex 14:10-12).

14.16.3.en: 3- Their murmuring because of the bitterness of the water at Marah and what the Lord did for them (Ex 15:24).

14.16.4.en: 4- The worship of the golden calf when Moses went up the mountain and delayed coming back to them, and their punishment (Ex 32:1).

14.16.5.en: 5- Their murmuring for food in the wilderness of Sin (Ex 16:2, 3).

14.16.7.en: 7- Their murmuring at Taberah and their punishment by the burning of the camp at its outskirts (ch. 11:1-3).

14.16.8.en: 8- The people's disobedience in keeping the manna until the second day (Ex 16:20).

14.16.9.en: 9- The people's disobedience in gathering manna on the Sabbath day (Ex 16:27, 28).

14.16.10.en: 10- And finally, their murmuring because of the words of the spies at Kadesh, the lofty (ch. 14:1-4).

14.17.0.en: God excepts Caleb from these punishments, and of course Joshua the son of Nun, but Caleb was the foremost in speaking. God is just and does not forget here the stand of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, whose conduct and faith differed from the conduct of the people, “another spirit,” and because he followed God fully, He will bring him into the land and give him a portion in it and an inheritance for his descendants after him.

14.18.0.en: The Amalekites dwell in the mountains and the Canaanites dwell beside the shores of the Mediterranean Sea. When the two, the Amalekites and the Canaanites, heard of the people of the children of Israel and their approach and the power of their God, they gathered in the valley in a state of preparation for war. Here God, in His love and fatherhood, warns the people against war and against meeting their enemies in the valley, and commands them to depart the next day into the wilderness, southward, in the direction of the Red Sea. Of course this command also agrees with God's punishment of the people and His intention that they not enter at this time.

14.18.1.en: If you refuse to obey God, you will deprive yourself of many blessings, and if you lose them you may not be able to make up for them. So seize every opportunity to draw near to God and enjoy His fellowship... Today is an opportunity to repent, to ask His mercies and to put away from you every evil.

14.19.s.en: (4) The Lord's speech about His punishment and the death of the ten spies

14.19.0.en: The previous speech was directed to Moses alone, but here God directs the words to Moses and Aaron together. The words in the coming verses come as a confirmation of God's justice and judgment, and they make clear to Moses and Aaron the reasons for this judgment. He begins His speech in an interrogative form, in disapproval of what the people had done, and says “How long,” an expression that indicates the abundance of His previous forgiveness and His long-suffering toward them, and also indicates the necessity of disciplining them because of their many murmurings.

14.20.0.en: God affirms here, in the form of an oath, “As I live,” that He will punish them with the very punishment they brought on themselves when in the revolt of their murmuring they said, “would God we had died in this wilderness” (v. 2). “In mine ears”: an expression God used, from which we all understand that everything a man says and utters with his tongue, or everything he thinks in his heart, is heard in the ears of God.

14.20.1.en: Take heed, beloved, and ask yourself: is everything you say, and God hears, pleasing before Him? And if it is not, you must take care and be precise, lest you bring wrath and anger upon yourself. Habit in words of thanksgiving keeps a man away from the circle of murmuring.

14.21.0.en: I lifted up my hand: an expression of the promise or oath that God promised to His people.

14.21.1.en: God's judgment was that everyone of the people over twenty years of age, that is, an adult and aware of what he says, would not enter this land but would die in the wilderness. God exempted from this punishment the two courageous spies, Joshua the disciple of Moses and Caleb, who spoke before the people to strengthen their resolve.

14.22.0.en: Likewise God also exempts those under 20 years of age, of whom the children of Israel had said that they would be a prey, captives and slaves to the Canaanites... They alone will enter this land and inherit it, know its goodness and excellence, and enjoy what the children of Israel despised. As for the rest, they will not be able to do any of this, for they will die in the wilderness.

14.23.0.en: Your whoredoms: your rebellion, your revolt and your murmuring.

14.23.1.en: However, the punishment will include your children also, in a measure, for because of your murmuring and your revolt your children will go on wandering in the wilderness for forty years instead of enjoying it now, until the whole present generation, those over twenty years of age, is consumed. God fixed the forty years on the ground that, since the days of their spying out the land came to forty days, the punishment for each day would be a whole year in which the people pay the price of their murmuring and know God's anger against them and His not walking with them and His distance from them. The exile of the children for 40 years in Sinai teaches them the heinousness of the sin of rebellion and its evil results, so that they obey God all their life.

14.24.0.en: The Lord affirms in this verse that everything He has spoken is irrevocable, describing His people, whom He regarded as a son and firstborn, as an evil people and a sinful congregation that conspired against its King and Father, “gathered together against” Him, rejecting His authority and not trusting in the power of His arm, which is able to destroy their enemies.

14.25.0.en: Made all the congregation to murmur: they made the people doubt and shook their faith in God.

14.25.1.en: As for the ten spies who caused the people to stumble, made them doubt and terrified them out of entering the land, God's judgment on them was swift and collective, for a plague struck them and the ten spies died because of their stumbling-block. As for Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, the punishment did not include them, for the just God gives every man according to his deserving.

14.25.2.en: There are people who are a source of stumbling, who weary the simple by their talk and gossip, perhaps about the Church or various matters, and there are also people who are a source of blessing and peace. Their words are few, but effective and useful for edification. So which of the two groups are you?!

14.26.0.en: The people listened to the words of Moses and felt their grave fault, for which they deserved God's punishment, and the people expressed their regret by their weeping. They wanted to atone for their fault by going up and fighting the Amalekites and the Canaanites, but they did not understand the Lord's purpose in their punishment and did not heed His warning about their enemies (v. 25).

14.27.0.en: Moses, the faithful shepherd and spiritual man experienced in the wisdom and purpose of God, warned the people not to do anything without God's command, for everyone who relies on his own thought and understanding without the divine plan will not succeed in it. In his warning he added that God was not with them and not in their midst in this war, and therefore they would not be victorious. He added that their enemies the Amalekites and the Canaanites were on alert and prepared for them, carrying their swords, that God would not intervene and would not protect His people from their enemies, and that their fate would be to be killed by the sword because of their fault and their turning back from God.

14.28.0.en: In pride and stubbornness the people did not listen to their leader and went up to meet their enemies without Moses, the guide, and without the ark of the covenant, which represents the presence of God. Since the people acted with folly and rashness and did not listen to the voice of their spiritual father, the Canaanites and the Amalekites, who were lying in wait for them on the mountain, came down on them, fought the people and inflicted on them the worst defeat and rout.

14.28.1.en: And discomfited them, even unto Hormah: Hormah is a place in the south of Palestine on the border of Edom, and it was called Hormah because there the Amalekites devoted them to destruction, that is, killed them.

14.28.2.en: Obedience to the spiritual father in the sacrament of confession is a duty, for the One speaking in the sacrament is the Holy Spirit. So do not be stubborn and harden your heart, lest you lose the blessing of obedience and the blessing of God Himself.

14.28.3.en: On the offerings of sacrifices, sins of ignorance and of presumption, and other laws
